title: SBI PO Prelims — Mock Test 8
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (CEC Gyanesh Kumar, T20 World Cup 2026, CPI inflation 1.7%, Operation Sindoor 2026, BioAsia 2026) — refreshable from admin CA pool.

questions.stem: If 'WORK' is coded as 'XPSL', how is 'PLAY' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: W→X, O→P, R→S, K→L. Apply to PLAY: P→Q, L→M, A→B, Y→Z → QMBZ.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'COLD' = 'DPME'. How is 'HEAT' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: C→D, O→P, L→M, D→E. Apply to HEAT: H→I, E→F, A→B, T→U → IFBU.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26, find sum of letter values in 'MATH'.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a girl, Naveen said, 'She is the daughter of my mother's only sister.' How is the girl related to Naveen?
questions.explanation: Naveen's mother's only sister = Naveen's maternal aunt. Daughter of maternal aunt = cousin.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If P + Q means P is the father of Q, P − Q means P is the brother of Q, and P × Q means P is the wife of Q, then the relation in 'A × B + C' is:
options: A is the mother of C
A is the aunt of C
A is the sister of C
A is the daughter of C
questions.explanation: A × B = A is the wife of B. B + C = B is the father of C. So A is the wife of C's father = A is C's mother.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A person walks 5 km North, then 4 km East, then 5 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net North-South: +5 − 5 = 0. Net East-West: +4 km East. Distance = 4 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are mammals.

Conclusions: I. All cats are mammals. II. Some mammals are cats.
questions.explanation: I: Cats ⊂ Dogs ⊂ Mammals ⟹ Cats ⊂ Mammals. TRUE. II: Cats ⊂ Mammals ⟹ some mammals are cats. TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some teachers are doctors. No doctor is a lawyer.

Conclusions: I. Some teachers are not lawyers. II. No teacher is a lawyer.
questions.explanation: I: Some teachers are doctors; no doctors are lawyers ⟹ those teachers are not lawyers. TRUE. II: 'No teacher is lawyer' is too strong — some teachers might still be lawyers. FALSE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A ≥ B, B > C, and C ≥ D, which is DEFINITELY TRUE?
questions.explanation: A ≥ B > C ≥ D. Since B > C is strict, A > D follows.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five cars A, B, C, D, E are parked in a row. C is to the right of B. A is to the left of B. E is to the right of C. D is between A and B. Who is at the extreme left?
questions.explanation: Order from left: A, D, B, C, E. A is at the extreme left.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 1 January 2027 is a Friday, what day was 1 January 2026?
questions.explanation: 2026 is not a leap year (365 days). 365 mod 7 = 1 odd day. Going BACK 1 day from Friday = Thursday.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: How many times do the hour and minute hands form a right angle in 24 hours?
questions.explanation: In 12 hours, the hands form right angles 22 times. In 24 hours: 44 times.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have NO painted face?
questions.explanation: Inner cubes = (n−2)³ = 3³ = 27.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.explanation: Position from left = Total − Position from right + 1 = 30 − 10 + 1 = 21st.

questions.stem: Average of 5 numbers is 30. If 2 are removed, average of remaining = 28. Find sum of removed numbers.

questions.stem: In which year was ISRO founded?
questions.passage_context: India's space programme has come a long way since its modest beginnings in the 1960s. ISRO, the Indian Space Research Organisation, was founded in 1969 with a vision of using space technology for national development. Early missions focused on satellite-based communication and weather forecasting. Over the decades, ISRO has mastered launch-vehicle technology, becoming one of only a handful of agencies capable of placing payloads into orbit. The Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) in 2014 made India the first country to reach Mars on its maiden attempt — and at remarkably low cost. The Chandrayaan missions have achieved a successful soft landing on the lunar south pole, a first in human history. Looking ahead, ISRO plans crewed missions, deep-space probes, and increased commercial launches. The agency's success demonstrates that ambitious science can be done on lean budgets with focused engineering and dedicated talent.
questions.explanation: Stated explicitly: 'ISRO ... founded in 1969.'
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'They were watching a movie.'
options: A movie was being watched by them.
A movie is watched by them.
A movie has been watched by them.
A movie was watched by them.
questions.explanation: Past-continuous active 'were V-ing' becomes past-continuous passive 'was/were being V3'.

questions.stem: Convert to active voice: 'The cake will be eaten by the children.'
options: The children will eat the cake.
The children have eaten the cake.
questions.explanation: Future-passive 'will be V3' becomes future-active 'will V'.

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the SECOND sentence.

(A) The success has earned global recognition.
(B) India's medical tourism industry has grown rapidly.
(C) Affordability and quality of care attract patients from around the world.
(D) Top hospitals in metro cities offer world-class facilities.
(E) The sector is expected to grow further with policy support.
questions.explanation: B (intro) → C (reasons) → D (specific facilities) → A (recognition) → E (future). 2nd = C.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the LAST sentence.

(A) Indian classical music has a rich tradition.
(B) Hindustani and Carnatic are its two major streams.
(C) Both share fundamental concepts but differ in style.
(D) Modern fusion artists blend classical with contemporary genres.
(E) This evolution ensures the tradition reaches new audiences.
questions.explanation: A (intro) → B (streams) → C (similarity) → D (modern fusion) → E (closing). Last = E.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
